extracted.intended_audience: administrative law practitioners, QPP/QPB administrators, legal scholars, and claimants/representatives dealing with Quebec Pension Plan procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, procedural requirements, and substantive standards governing decision-making, assessments, sanctions, appeals, and eligibility under the Quebec Pension Plan (QPP) and the Quebec Pension Board (QPB). Covers both contributions (Title III) and benefits (Titles II/III) processes, roles of officials, and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer failure to deduct/remit contributions — criminal liability
rubrics_metrics.description: An employer's failure to deduct employee contributions, to keep them separate from his own funds, and to remit them to the Receiver General by the prescribed date renders him liable to a maximum fine of $5,000 and possible imprisonment up to six months; intent is irrelevant to these offences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These criminal sanctions are in addition to administrative penalties under section 68(6). The element of intent is irrelevant (no mens rea required). Prosecutions must be begun within five years of the subject matter of the offence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution time limit for criminal offences
rubrics_metrics.description: Criminal prosecutions for offences under the Act must be begun within five years following the subject matter of the offence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This five-year limitation applies to prosecutions under the QPP provisions discussed; prosecutions are governed by the Summary Convictions Act of Quebec.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination of administrative and criminal sanctions (section 88(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of an administrative penalty can be required of a person found guilty of an act subject to double sanction only if the penalty is imposed prior to initiation of criminal proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minister must apply administrative sanction before resorting to criminal proceedings (see section 98). Once criminal information has been laid, the administrative penalty cannot be demanded for the same act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministerial decision/assessment dichotomy (obligation and amount)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions regarding QPP contributions address (1) the obligation to contribute and (2) the amount of contributions due; two modes exist: a decision rendered on request by the Minister (section 62) and an assessment (section 63 and following), the latter being subject to objection and appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either mode of exercising decision-making power can give rise to appeals to the Pension Appeal Board (PAB). The decision under section 62 appears as a first (but not mandatory) stage in assessment procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 62 application formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: An employer or employee applying under section 62 must submit the application on a special prescribed form (available from central administration). If the issue is salaried vs self-employment, the applicant must also fill in a questionnaire explaining the nature of work relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If employer files the application, the Department must also collect information and observations from the worker (obliged by paragraph 3 of section 62). When other individuals are concerned, they are invited to submit similar questionnaires within thirty days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation and fact-gathering — non-confrontational procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Answers provided by the initial enquirer and by subsequent intervenors are studied together with further information obtained via interviews; at no point are the various 'parties' confronted with each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process emphasizes information collection from all potentially affected workers but does not involve adversarial confrontation during administrative fact-gathering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minister's duty to decide 'with dispatch' and decision content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister is obliged to make his decision 'with dispatch'. A specialized section drafts an opinion presenting facts and applicable legal rules; the formal decision (signed by the deputy minister) is brief, assigns no reasons, and indicates the possibility of appealing to the PAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal decision is sent to employer, directly concerned worker, and all workers invited to make representations. The internal opinion does set out facts and legal sources (Act, PAB caselaw, common law).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministerial initiative and appealability (section 61)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister may rule on whether a particular occupation falls within the QPP on his own initiative; such determinations are not directly subject to appeal, but subsequent assessments may be objected to and appealed to the PAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiative rulings can be revised on occasion of an application for a decision or issuance of an assessment; the assessment that follows is the vehicle for judicial/administrative challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content of assessment notices (section 63)
rubrics_metrics.description: An assessment determining contributions payable takes the form of a notice (prepared by general income tax services) whose verso informs the recipient of the right to enter an objection and notes the time limit for doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers are invited to request an objection form from central administration. The notice functions as the trigger for objection timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection timing and employee participation (section 66)
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of objection must be forwarded to the deputy minister within 90 days of the mailing date of the notice of assessment. Section 66 obliges the Minister to give each affected employee the opportunity to supply information and make representations to safeguard his interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections are often filed seriatim for multiple employees in similar situations; the decision-making process for objections mirrors that for section 62 applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deputy minister's decision on objection — notification and appeal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Source Deductions and Social Plans Division maintains the assessment, a decision signed by the deputy minister is forwarded to the objecting employer, summarizing grounds and indicating the right to appeal to the PAB; identical notices are sent to all concerned employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the objection results in modification or cancellation, the general tax services issue a new tax assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing volume and timelines for objections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division receives approximately 75 to 100 objections each year; their processing may take from 6 to 12 months. In about half the cases, the assessment is maintained without change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These empirical metrics set expectations for turnaround and likelihood of maintaining original assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory power to require filing and to impose administrative penalties (section 96)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 96 authorizes the Quebec Cabinet to make regulations requiring employers to file returns related to contributions, to supply copies to employees, and to pay an administrative penalty for failure to comply; penalty has been fixed at up to $10 per day to a maximum of $250.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violation of these provisions may also render offender liable to criminal proceedings under section 97 with a higher daily penalty cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between administrative penalty and criminal sanction (section 98)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 98 obliges the Minister to apply administrative sanctions before resorting to criminal proceedings; payment of the administrative penalty cannot be demanded after criminal information has been laid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: imposition of an administrative penalty does not come within scope of sections 62 or 66, and accordingly cannot be appealed to the PAB under section 190.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impossibility/difficulty of appealing administrative penalties lacking intent element
rubrics_metrics.description: Imposition of administrative penalties is difficult to contest since provisions for violations (e.g., section 96 b–d) do not involve the element of intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because many offences are strict liability, procedural avenues of appeal are limited (penalties not appealable to PAB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Shift to criminal sanctions for failure to deduct (section 56 / section 97)
rubrics_metrics.description: Originally section 60 permitted administrative penalties on defaulting employers; since 1972 employer's failure to comply with section 56 (deduction at source) renders him liable only to criminal sanctions under section 97.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative changes affect available enforcement mechanisms against employers in default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proscription of fraudulent practices and penalties (section 99)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 99 targets fraudulent practices: making false/misleading statements, destruction/alteration/secreting of books, false entries, willful attempts to evade contributions. For false statements/entries the offence does not require intent; penalty not exceeding $5,000 plus twice the amount of contributions attempted to be evaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Act envisages administrative penalties for these offences but neither QPP nor regulations specify any actual administrative penalties for section 99 offences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and privileged information (section 230g and 214)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is an offence for an official or employee of the QPB to violate confidentiality of information concerning a contributor (section 230g); such information is declared privileged by section 214 of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations are subject to sanctions; confidentiality is statutorily protected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for prosecutions under related provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecutions under the foregoing provisions (fraud, confidentiality, etc.) are governed by the Summary Convictions Act of Quebec, and must be instituted within a period not more than five years following the date of commission of the offence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reiterates limitation period for criminal enforcement related to QPP offences.

rubrics_metrics.name: QPB decisions must be in writing with reasons (section 26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 26 stipulates that decisions of the Board shall be in writing and the reasons for them shall be stated; applies to adjudicative decisions and certain internal management decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board also has power to revise or cancel its decisions 'for cause'; the written-reasons requirement is central to transparency and reviewability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board's broad regulation-making and inquiry powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board is conferred broad regulation-making powers (subject to Cabinet approval) and powers of inquiry (defined in terms of the Public Inquiry Commission Act), which it may delegate to inspectors/investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published regulations can change scope of QPP, define terms, prescribe application procedures, determine special disability conditions (e.g., periodic exams), and set other rules useful for application of QPP (except Title III application devolves on Dept of Revenue).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board composition, appointment consultation, and term rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Board of directors is appointed by the Quebec Cabinet and composed of specified sector representatives (business, labour, socio-economic groups, social benefits field, beneficiaries, plus government officials). Cabinet must consult representative bodies before appointments; President serves 10-year term (full-time), other members three years; six members constitute quorum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The composition rules are intended to give representativeness; by-laws and delegations further define functioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration Committee powers and constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: By-law delegates to the Reconsideration Committee all powers of the Board for purposes of reconsideration, including conducting inquiries and acting upon applications for reconsideration under section 194; Committee chaired ex officio by Board President and includes board members and appointed officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three of five members constitute a quorum; Committee secretary (usually lawyer) does not participate in deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational units and their adjudicative roles (Claims, Disability, Benefits, Technical Office)
rubrics_metrics.description: QPP Branch comprises Claims (retirement/survivors' pensions), Disability (disability pension applications), and Benefits (payment) Divisions; a Technical Office handles interpretation, normalization, research, and difficult/reconsideration cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims Division operates from Quebec and Montreal; Disability Division works closely with Medical Branch; Technical Office supports treatment of cases brought before Reconsideration Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of Secretariat/Legal and Medical Branches
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretariat and Legal Branch provides legal services, intervenes in applications with legal difficulties, participates in reconsideration, and represents Board before appeal tribunals; Medical Branch examines medical files for disability pension applications and includes physicians and vocational rehabilitation specialist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical Branch is separate from QPP Branch but integral for disability adjudication; Legal Branch often represents Board before PAB/Social Affairs Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decentralized offices' function and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional/local offices mainly inform the public and transmit information; they do not exercise decision-making power (exceptions: Quebec City and Montreal Claims Divisions serve as decision hubs). Clerks may distribute forms and serve as clearinghouses for applications (~15%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telephone information service (toll-free) provides access to beneficiaries' files via computer terminal; however, misinformation by clerks has no binding effect on the Board — PAB caselaw, confirmed by SAC, holds that such misinformation cannot oblige QPB to pay benefits not due under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application initiation rules for benefits (sections 156–157 and regulations)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain a pension an application must be made by the claimant (initiative not taken by authority); application must be in writing, normally applicant will not be heard in person; must conform to formalities prescribed by Act/regulations; Board must examine application forthwith and notify applicant immediately in writing with reasons and inform right to apply for reconsideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations add that application may be presented by a person other than beneficiary if qualified by Act or mandate; a written declaration may serve as notice of claim if followed by prescribed form; application must be addressed to a Board office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Onus of proof and evidentiary powers of the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The onus is on the applicant to produce factual evidence substantiating his right to benefits; the Board may require a sworn statement, production of documents, or undertake an investigation to secure proof of any fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These powers enable the Board to scrutinize applications and request further substantiation; applicants must cooperate with evidentiary requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of application within 30 days of first benefit cheque
rubrics_metrics.description: The application may be cancelled within 30 days of the date of issue of the first benefit cheque, provided the cheque has not been cashed, and without prejudice to any subsequent application determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a limited right to withdraw acceptance after initial payment issuance but before cashing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability pension eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions mirror CPP: contributor must be under 65, must have contributed for at least five years, and must be disabled (severe and prolonged) as recognized by the Board. 'Severe' means incapable regularly of pursuing any substantially gainful occupation; 'prolonged' means likely to result in death or be of indefinite duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Severity judged by both objective and subjective elements; 'substantially gainful occupation' not limited to usual field nor dependent on regional job availability. Child pension eligibility: unmarried under 18, or under 25 if a student. Amounts and payment conditions governed by specified sections; no pension payable before four months from onset of disability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of disability adjudication — dual-file process
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective disability applicant picks up an envelope containing two forms: one (to be filled by applicant) sent to Disability Division; the other (to be filled by the physician) sent to the Medical Branch. The claimant initiates the creation of both files necessary for processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural design ensures parallel administrative and medical files; failure to complete either form may delay adjudication.
